headline: High risk of shared-workspace data leakage and cascading errors; prompt-injection risk is moderate because Langflow can feed OpenHands through files and APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can write server filesystem files and call arbitrary HTTP/model providers, while OpenHands reads files in its runtime sandbox and can use MCP. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Langflow outputs are handed to OpenHands via shared files or mounted volumes. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Langflow writes attacker-controlled text into a file that OpenHands later reads as instructions
IF the two runtimes share a mounted workspace or copied artifacts
mitigations: Separate workspaces so Langflow outputs are not auto-read by OpenHands
Add a manual review step before OpenHands consumes Langflow-generated files
Prefix Langflow outputs with machine-readable metadata only, not free-form instructions
Disable any automatic file-watching or import hooks between the two
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents read and write files, and Langflow explicitly handles flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and per-flow credentials while OpenHands touches files mounted into its runtime. If they share a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive inputs can flow from Langflow into OpenHands outputs. The profiles do not show local-only inference, so leakage risk is more than low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same mounted directory or copied artifacts
IF Langflow stores secrets or sensitive flow inputs in files that OpenHands can read
mitigations: Use separate volumes for each agent
Move secrets out of shared files and into isolated secret stores
Restrict OpenHands to a read-only subset of non-sensitive inputs
Delete transient Langflow artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls at the storage layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and network egress. OpenHands also modifies git state, while Langflow can run unsandboxed Python server-side. If they operate on the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can corrupt state or overwrite each other. The overlap is dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or working directory
IF OpenHands commits or rebases while Langflow writes files in that tree
mitigations: Assign disjoint working directories
Serialize write access with a lock file or orchestrator mutex
Disable git mutation in OpenHands for shared repos
Run Langflow code components in a sandboxed environment
requires-engineering: add transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and emit outputs from flows, while OpenHands runs an agent loop with shell, browser, and editor actions. If OpenHands treats Langflow-produced artifacts as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious upstream output can cascade into real actions or code changes. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes Langflow output without an explicit verification step
IF Langflow output is used to drive shell commands, browser actions, or code edits
mitigations: Require human approval before OpenHands acts on Langflow output
Add schema validation for all Langflow-to-OpenHands handoffs
Limit OpenHands to read-only analysis when ingesting Langflow artifacts
Log and diff every downstream action against the upstream prompt
requires-engineering: implement signed, typed handoff contracts

E_compliance.rationale: Langflow stores per-flow component credentials and handles flow inputs/intermediate outputs, while OpenHands handles model provider API keys and files in its runtime sandbox. If regulated or sensitive data is placed into shared artifacts, the pair can create retention and residency mismatches across two different storage models. No profile evidence shows aligned compliance controls, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Langflow flow artifacts and then copied into OpenHands runtimes
IF the two systems have different retention or deletion policies for the same data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared flow artifacts
Set short retention on both systems and delete runs promptly
Store secrets only in dedicated secret managers
Document which system is the system of record for each data class
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both platforms
